sanskrit_verse:
अनिर्णीते विवादे तु विप्रलब्धो भवेन् नृपः ।
जयदानं समं न स्यात् तस्मात् कार्याणि निर्णयेत् ॥
transliteration: anirṇīte vivāde tu vipralabdho bhaven nṛpaḥ / jayadānaṃ samaṃ na syāt tasmāt kāryāṇi nirṇayet //
sph_interpretive_translation: When a dispute remains unresolved, the ruler becomes deceived; hence, there can be no equitable distribution of victory or reward. Therefore, matters must be decisively resolved.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority rests in resolution, not ambiguity
Causation arises from clarity, not confusion
Consciousness alignment occurs through lawful completion

supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, prolonged unresolved disputes compromise the sovereign's capacity to uphold dharma. The court must prioritize finality and clarity to prevent systemic deception and ensure that rewards or outcomes align with truth-consciousness, not subjective interpretation.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality establishes that unresolved disputes cloud judgment and impede dharma. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals that delay leads to distortion. Proportional responsibility lies in executing timely resolution. Non-punitive reality rule affirms that justice is about restoring clarity, not inflicting consequence.
